To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pure annihilation form-factor is dominated by a single pole, that the large-N approximation enhances its contribution to the decay rate, that PCAC has to either be violated or the non-leading terms in the large-N expansion have to be included, and that a moderate violation of PCAC is sufficient to reproduce the experimental branching ratio for the decay D0 → K0π+π−.
(i) the annihilation form factor for D0 → K0 ϕ is small and (ii) it cannot be enhanced to the observed value by the large-N expansion.

the annihilation form-factor associated with the D0 → K0φ decay is large, and that it can be described in the chiral SU(3)_L × SU(3)_R × U(1)_V framework only if the chiral limit is not taken and the chiral symmetry is strongly broken at the scale q^2 = m^2_D.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the D0 → K0 ϕ decay mode, in the framework of the chiral SU(3)xSU(3) Lagrangian and the large-N expansion.
the evaluation of the form factor for the decay D0 → K0 ϕ, using the single pole approximation and experimental data on the ϕ → K K decay.
the study of the weak form factor associated to the pure annihilation decays D0 → K0 ϕ and F+ → ρ+ π+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
annihilation is not suppressed in the D-meson decays.
factorization of the annihilation form factors is not supported by the present data.
the data are consistent with the large-N limit of the standard model, but not with the large-N approximation of the standard model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pure annihilation decays are suppressed in the chiral limit, but large-N corrections and violations of PCAC may enhance them considerably.
factorization of the D0 → K0π0 matrix element is not valid in the pure annihilation channel D0 → K−ϕ.
the annihilation decay D→Kϕ is not suppressed in the chiral limit, but it is strongly suppressed if one assumes the validity of the single pole approximation and the large N limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the large-N limit is very sensitive to the way the large-q2 behavior is extrapolated to the large-N limit and that the large-N expansion is not a good approximation in the presence of strong PCAC violation.
the annihilation form factor is very small and that the observed D0 → K0π0 decay is due to the D → K form factor.
the large branching ratio for the D0 → K0 ϕ decay can be explained by a moderate breaking of factorization or PCAC, but not by a large-N expansion.
